page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre; page number top right. Main text in full width paragraphs: an italic passage at top, then a woodcut plate of coins with its caption below, then a chapter heading and text at the bottom. Marginal note in the left margin beside the last lines.

main_text.p: Atque infrà: Καὶ τῇ μὲν δεξιᾷ χρεὶ κατέχει τὸν σαυ-ρὸν, ὡς Σιβυλλης ἐστι νεκρλεῖν τὸν βασιλέα ὅταν Ꞓ τὸ σῆμα φορεῖ: Et dextrâ quidem manu tenet crucem, sicut solenne est teneri ab Imperatore, quoties & Stemma fert, id est diadema. Ab hoc ritu etiamnunc crucifer ille globus inter Sacri illius Imperij insignia: quod tu nunc Rudolphe Caesar per tot inclytos maiores ad te missum tenes, tenebisq; diu (ita voueo) bono Christiani orbis.
[woodcut plate of Constantinian and Byzantine coins, not transcribed as text]
main_text.head: CAP. XVII. Laudatiuncula Crucis.
main_text.p: Ω ξύλον μακαρειστὸν, ἐν ᾧ θεὸς ἐξετάνυσθη. O lignum felix, in quo Deus ipse pependit.

page.notes: The plate of coins shows labelled coins (ANNO XXXX, CONOB, VICTORIA AVG, CONSTANTINI AVG, FILIAVS, etc.) and is described, not transcribed. The first Greek line is copied as far as legible; the marginal reference "Sibylla apud Sozomen. II. cap. 1." stands in the left margin. The large initial S of "Sed" is a woodcut initial. Some Greek letters at the top are uncertain.
